messages:
deploy-bot: [AUTOMATED ALERT] Canary rollout r5.2.1 -> eu-west-1 showing sustained 5xx spike. http_5xx_rate > 20% for the last 3m across canary set. commit=abc1234 view: https://ci.redwood.internal/runs/3321

maya: seeing it. hitting grafana now. tagging oncall. @ops-sre please confirm paging policy fired?

incident-bot: Paging oncall rotation (eng-oncall) — incident severity: P2. Escalation: send page to @priya then @liam. Link: https://incidents.redwood/internal/1776543210

priya: got the page, joining. Maya — any idea if this is app-level or infra?

maya: initial look suggests requests are routing to canary pods which are healthy on k8s but returning 503s. logs show upstream errors in the new scheduler module. grabbing pod logs:

maya: ```
kubectl -n inference logs canary-69f4b8 -c runtime
2026-03-11T22:03:12Z ERROR upstream_fetch failed status=503 service=kv-cache
2026-03-11T22:03:12Z WARN eviction loop triggered: cache miss storm
```

kai: I'm seeing a feedback loop between the autoscaler and the new scheduler: scale-up -> cache warmup failures -> high latency -> LB returns 503 -> autoscaler scales down older pods. looks like a bad interaction with the new scale policy (burst=on).

liam: tagging @deploy-bot — can we pause the staged rollout routing to canary? Need to stop traffic to this variant and failover to baseline.

deploy-bot: Executing traffic tilt rollback — removing 30% traffic from canary -> baseline. Operation queued.

maya: tilt command done, but 503s still at ~12% overall. Some dedicated customers on eu-west report errors (CS ticket numbers: CS-1204, CS-1207).

cs-bot: Notified customer-success about CS-1204 and CS-1207. Sending templated update.
messages_addendum:
priya: rolling restart of canary pods seems to reduce error bursts but not fix. I suspect autoscaler aggressive TTL + new scheduler kv cache eviction causes cache storm.

maya: we have a configuration flag ff.new-scheduler.enabled=true in the rollout. Propose flipping the kill-switch to false for eu-west and then do a rollback of the canary image if errors persist.

kai: agreed. prepping commands.

maya: executing feature-flag kill-switch:

maya: ```
redwood flags set ff.new-scheduler.enabled false --env=prod --region=eu-west-1 --scope=rollout-3321
```

deploy-bot: Feature flag update acknowledged. Propagating to edge (eu-west-1).

maya: after FF flip, 503s dropped to ~3% in last 60s. baseline latency stable. Good so far.

kai: still seeing a few canary pods with old image that keep flapping; recommend rolling back the release to r5.2.0 for eu-west to be safe.

liam: if FF flip stabilizes, do we need full rollback? cs reported 2 paying dedicated customers experienced errors for ~6 minutes. ops needs a clean rollback plan in case of regression.

maya: rolling back just the canary slice now:

maya: ```
redwood deploy rollback --to r5.2.0 --region eu-west-1 --target=canary --reason="503 spike during staged rollout"
kubectl rollout status deploy/inference-canary -n inference
```

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated. Job id: rb-2026-1776543210.

kai: rollback completed on canary pods. canary image now r5.2.0. verifying metrics.

maya: metrics show http_5xx_rate back to baseline <1% across region. Latency normal. CS notified that issue resolved and root cause being investigated.

ops-sre: Paging closure checklist: verify all canary pods stable, confirm no queued rollouts for same tag, ensure autoscaler policy reverted to conservative profile.

priya: autoscaler policy for rollout-3321 has been set to conservative (burst disabled) and a PR is in flight to add a safety knob to avoid scale-down during cache-warmup. PR: https://git.redwood/pull/4042

liam: handoff — I'm taking post-incident follow-up and postmortem. Summary: canary rollout r5.2.1 triggered a kv-cache eviction storm when combined with aggressive autoscaler burst policy, causing 503s and impacting a small number of dedicated customers. Mitigations: FF kill-switch flipped, canary rollback to r5.2.0, autoscaler policy adjusted.

liam: action items assigned:
- maya: gather logs + timeline (due in 2 hrs)
- kai: validate PR for autoscaler safety knob and test plan (due tomorrow)
- priya: confirm alert thresholds and add runbook step for FF kill-switch (due in 24h)
- cs-bot: follow-up customer comms with root-cause note (in progress)

cs-bot: Sent follow-up to affected customers: "We mitigated the issue and rolled back the canary; a postmortem will be shared."

liam: handing off to next oncall in 90m. If you need me I’ll be reachable via this thread. Closing page for now. :white_check_mark:
